key_insight: DreamTrue makes robot video prediction more action-faithful by conditioning on rendered action trajectories and correcting model bias with counterfactual post-training. This helps the world model stay physically plausible while better matching what the robot actually does across different embodiments.
problem_solved: The paper addresses two core issues in robot world models: imperfect calibration that causes poor action following, and dataset bias toward successful interactions that makes models overpredict success and underrepresent failures.
method: Render robot action trajectories into image-space conditions so the model can more accurately follow actions across different robot bodies.
Apply offline geometric calibration to reduce the effect of misalignment and improve cross-embodiment consistency.
Use counterfactual post-training to expose the model to unsuccessful or alternative outcomes, improving realism and reducing success bias.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves the reliability of learned robot world models for planning, simulation, and policy training. It is especially useful when working with diverse robot datasets that contain noisy calibration or limited failure examples.

paper_title: DreamTrue: Action-Faithful Robot World Model with Counterfactual Post-Training
